title: Crypto CTF Walkthroughs — A Practical Triage Loop (Toy)

questions.question: What is a good first step when you see an unknown-looking ciphertext string?
options: Validate the encoding (hex/base64) and decode layers
Assume it is AES-GCM and search for the nonce
Guess the key by brute force without decoding
questions.explanation: Correct decoding prevents wasted effort and corrupted assumptions.

questions.question: Why are GCD checks useful in RSA CTF tasks with multiple moduli?
options: They can instantly reveal shared prime factors from bad key generation
questions.explanation: If two moduli share a prime, gcd exposes it immediately.

questions.question: What does a single-byte XOR breaker typically rely on?
options: Trying all 256 keys and scoring plaintext likelihood
questions.explanation: Single-byte XOR is small enough to brute force; scoring selects plausible plaintext.

questions.question: If gcd(n1, n2) returns a non-trivial factor p, what does that imply?
options: n1 and n2 share p, so at least one modulus is factorable immediately
RSA is broken for all keys
questions.explanation: A shared prime indicates catastrophic key generation failure.

questions.question: After factoring n = p*q, what is the next standard step to decrypt textbook RSA?
options: Compute d = e^{-1} mod (p−1)(q−1) and then m = c^d mod n
Hash the ciphertext to get plaintext
Use CBC decryption with IV = p
questions.explanation: With p and q you can compute φ(n) and invert e to get d.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a triage loop in crypto challenges?
options: Run cheap, high-yield checks first before deep attacks
Guarantee a solution in one step
questions.explanation: Triage prioritizes quick wins and prevents time sinks.

questions.question: Which mistake commonly causes “nonsense” plaintext in early attempts?
options: Decoding with the wrong format (treating base64 as hex or vice versa)
questions.explanation: Incorrect decoding corrupts data and leads to false conclusions.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to skip basic RSA sanity checks and jump to advanced attacks?
options: You can miss catastrophic configuration failures that solve the problem immediately
RSA moduli cannot be checked with gcd
questions.explanation: Many CTF tasks hinge on simple mistakes; basic checks can solve them quickly.
